claim: Having a formal onboarding procedure for new lab members can lead to a happier and more productive working environment.
source: Having a formal onboarding procedure for new lab members can lead to a happier and more productive working environment.
evidence: This is a general assertion presented in the abstract without specific experimental data, citations, or detailed supporting evidence in the manuscript.

claim: Providing new members with a list of essential items they should receive or have access to can accelerate adjustment to the lab.
source: Providing new members with a list of essential items they should receive or have access to can accelerate adjustment to the lab (see Box 1 for an example).
evidence: This is a recommendation based on logical reasoning about onboarding practices, without specific experimental data or citations.

claim: Universities or individual departments may offer 'orientation checklists' for new employees and students.
source: While we have provided a basic checklist for new lab members, it is important to note that universities or individual departments may also offer 'orientation checklists' for new employees and students.
evidence: This draws from general knowledge about institutional practices in academic settings.

claim: University orientation information will not be specific to the lab environment and may lack important details.
source: however, we suggest not relying on this information entirely as it will not be specific to the lab environment and may lack important details.
evidence: This is an inference based on the general nature of university-wide versus lab-specific information.

claim: Including typical milestones and timelines in the onboarding package can help ensure that the expectations of the new lab member are aligned with those of the PIs.
source: We recommend including the typical milestones and timelines expected for incoming lab members within the onboarding package; this can help ensure that the expectations of the new lab member are aligned with those of the PIs.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on logical inference about the benefits of clear communication.

claim: Check-in meetings between the PI and the new lab member are crucial to define and evaluate an employee's short- and long-term goals, improving workflow optimization.
source: These meetings are crucial to define and evaluate an employee's short- and long-term goals, improving workflow optimization.
evidence: This is an assertion based on inference about the benefits of regular meetings, without specific data or citations.

claim: PhD students must achieve specific milestones before the university awards their diploma.
source: Agreed-upon timelines are particularly useful for PhD students who must achieve specific milestones before the university awards their diploma.
evidence: This draws from established knowledge about PhD program requirements in academic institutions.

claim: PhD timelines can include department-specific requirements, such as coursework and teaching responsibilities, and goals specific to the research project.
source: PhD timelines can include department-specific requirements, such as coursework and teaching responsibilities, and goals specific to the research project (see example in Box 1).
evidence: This is based on general knowledge of typical PhD program structures.

claim: Constructing timelines for postdocs and technicians can increase productivity.
source: To increase productivity, PIs can construct a similar timeline for other lab members, such as postdocs and technicians.
evidence: This is a speculative assertion about the benefits of timelines without supporting data.

claim: PIs often have different views on certain aspects of the scientific process, such as publishing, collaborations, and conferences.
source: PIs often have different views on certain aspects of the scientific process, such as publishing, collaborations, and conferences.
evidence: This is based on general knowledge about variability in scientific practices and preferences among PIs.

claim: PI attitudes about scientific processes tend to be assumed and not formally stated.
source: However, these attitudes tend to be assumed and not formally stated.
evidence: This is an inference based on observations about typical lab communication practices.

claim: Communicating the lab's scientific policies and core values as part of the onboarding package can help new (and existing) members be more aware of the PI's expectations.
source: Communicating the lab's scientific policies and core values as part of the onboarding package can help new (and existing) members be more aware of the PI's expectations.
evidence: This is an inference about the benefits of clear communication without specific supporting data.

claim: Striking a proper work-life balance can be challenging for many in academic research labs.
source: Striking a proper work-life balance can be challenging for many in academic research labs.
evidence: This is supported by the survey data cited in the following sentences.

claim: Approximately 40% of PhD students were dissatisfied with their work-life balance.
source: Surveys of PhD students (pre- and post-pandemic) have found that approximately 40% were dissatisfied with their work-life balance, 76% worked more than 40 hours per week, and one in three students were at risk of developing a mental health disorder (Woolston, 2019; Levecque et al., 2017; Forrester, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by cited survey data from multiple sources.

claim: 76% of PhD students worked more than 40 hours per week.
source: Surveys of PhD students (pre- and post-pandemic) have found that approximately 40% were dissatisfied with their work-life balance, 76% worked more than 40 hours per week, and one in three students were at risk of developing a mental health disorder (Woolston, 2019; Levecque et al., 2017; Forrester, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by cited survey data from multiple sources.

claim: One in three PhD students were at risk of developing a mental health disorder.
source: Surveys of PhD students (pre- and post-pandemic) have found that approximately 40% were dissatisfied with their work-life balance, 76% worked more than 40 hours per week, and one in three students were at risk of developing a mental health disorder (Woolston, 2019; Levecque et al., 2017; Forrester, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by cited survey data from multiple sources.

claim: Postdocs, faculty, and staff face similar challenges to PhD students regarding work-life balance.
source: Postdocs, faculty, and staff face similar challenges (Woolston, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Woolston, 2020.

claim: 30% of faculty reported regularly feeling exhausted in a 2020 survey.
source: Indeed, 30% of faculty reported regularly feeling exhausted in a 2020 survey (Businesswire, 2021)
evidence: This claim is supported by cited survey data.

claim: Research vivarium personnel reported suffering from workplace-related stress due to long hours.
source: and technicians, such as research vivarium personnel, also reported suffering from workplace-related stress due to long hours (Murray et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Murray et al., 2020.

claim: Providing realistic expectations regarding working hours and vacation time in the onboarding document can help mitigate burnout-inducing scenarios.
source: Providing realistic expectations regarding working hours and vacation time in the onboarding document can help mitigate burnout-inducing scenarios.
evidence: This is an inference based on the relationship between clear expectations and stress reduction.

claim: Starting conversations about work-life balance early – when someone first joins the lab – can help alleviate some of the stress of balancing work and personal life.
source: Starting these conversations early – when someone first joins the lab – can help alleviate some of the stress of balancing work and personal life.
evidence: This is an inference about the benefits of early communication without specific supporting data.

claim: Most labs do not have dedicated staff responsible for making stock solutions, managing laboratory animals or cell cultures, and keeping equipment in working condition.
source: Most labs do not have dedicated staff responsible for making stock solutions, managing laboratory animals or cell cultures, and keeping equipment in working condition.
evidence: This is based on general knowledge about typical lab staffing structures.

claim: Clearly outlining the division of labor for lab maintenance tasks can help the lab run more smoothly and equitably.
source: Clearly outlining the division of labor for these kinds of tasks can help the lab run more smoothly and equitably.
evidence: This is an inference about the benefits of clear task assignment.

claim: Women are more likely than men to assume or be delegated to support roles regardless of their job description.
source: Women are more likely than men to assume or be delegated to support roles regardless of their job description (Dishman, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dishman, 2015.

claim: Eliminating ambiguity surrounding general lab maintenance will help minimize burdens that can take away from research productivity, which disproportionately impacts women and people of color.
source: Eliminating ambiguity surrounding general lab maintenance will help minimize burdens that can take away from research productivity, which disproportionately impacts women and people of color.
evidence: This is an inference combining the cited information about gender disparities with reasoning about the impact of clear task assignment.

claim: PIs can make lab managers and technicians responsible for supervising lab tasks, empowering them to enforce obligations that other members of the group have agreed to take on.
source: PIs can also make lab managers and technicians responsible for supervising lab tasks, empowering them to enforce obligations that other members of the group have agreed to take on.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on inference about effective lab management strategies.

claim: A single onboarding package is unlikely to comprehensively address every new employee's unique needs and situations.
source: A single onboarding package is unlikely to comprehensively address every new employee's unique needs and situations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the diversity of individual circumstances and needs.

claim: Many tasks, practices, and tools are common to research environments.
source: However, many tasks, practices, and tools are common to research environments.
evidence: This is based on general knowledge about research lab operations.

claim: It is valuable to construct a basic onboarding template that can be expanded to include job-specific considerations to help new members integrate into the lab smoothly and quickly.
source: It is valuable to construct a basic onboarding template that can be expanded to include job-specific considerations to help new members integrate into the lab smoothly and quickly.
evidence: This is an inference about the benefits of a flexible onboarding approach.

claim: An onboarding package is a living document that requires time and effort from the PI and all lab members to remain relevant.
source: An onboarding package is a living document that requires time and effort from the PI and all lab members to remain relevant.
evidence: This is an inference about the need for ongoing maintenance of documentation.

claim: The energy invested in constructing detailed onboarding practices will pay off in increased productivity and job satisfaction in academic research.
source: We are confident that the energy invested in constructing detailed onboarding practices will pay off in increased productivity and job satisfaction in academic research.
evidence: This is a speculative assertion about the benefits of onboarding practices without specific supporting data.
